thread:
maria: heads up — noticed ~2% of requests to our eu-west ALBs are returning the default cert instead of the customer cert. happens only when traffic egresses through NAT pool A.
cheng: ugh. any pattern on clienthello SNI?
maria: yes, server logs show ClientHello without SNI on the ALB side for a subset. tracing shows connections coming from a handful of egress IPs in NAT pool A.
oliver: that sounds like a NAT hairpin/translate issue — maybe TCP proxy preserves some TLS record fragmentation and ALB picks up first fragment?
maria: maybe. reproducer: `curl --resolve api.prod.redwood.example:443:10.2.3.4 https://api.prod.redwood.example/health --verbose` shows ALPN+SNI on some attempts, but on failing runs ALB picks default cert.
cheng: can you paste a failing openssl dump? `openssl s_client -connect alb-eu-west:443 -servername api.prod.redwood.example -msg`
maria: pasted below:
-----BEGIN OPENSSL_OUTPUT-----
>>> TLS 1.3, Handshake, ClientHello
    Version: 1.3
    Random: (redacted)
    Extensions: server_name: api.prod.redwood.example
>>> TLS 1.3, Handshake, ClientHello (fragment)
-----END OPENSSL_OUTPUT-----
cheng: interesting — fragment seen. ALB might be reading only first TCP segment which occasionally contains only part of ClientHello without SNI ext. If NAT device resegments packets, the ALB could see the wrong boundary.
oncall-liz: @maria assigning to oncall to investigate. can we confirm this is correlated with NAT pool A EIP rotation at 03:00UTC?
maria: yes — correlation matches maintenance window when pool A briefly reassigns EIPs between nodes.
oliver: workaround idea: add a TCP connection reassembly setting on the NAT nodes or pin flows to avoid resegmentation. also we can set ALB listener TLS policy to always read full handshake? not sure ALB exposes that.
cheng: ALB is managed — no reassembly knobs. We can try: 1) force clients to send SNI+ALPN in first segment (hard) 2) prevent EIP reassignments during peak 3) change NAT path so symmetric flow remains on same NAT instance.
infra-bot: @maria created ticket INF-4321: investigate SNI-less ClientHello arriving at ALB from NAT pool A. Priority: P1.
deploy-bot: rolling back the last NAT config change is scheduled if INF-4321 owners mark `rollback:true`.
oncall-liz: for immediate mitigation, can we add a stricter Host header validation in the app to reduce impact when default cert is served? it's not ideal but limits exposure.
maria: agreed. i'll add a quick ingress rule that rejects requests where Host != api.prod.redwood.example at the edge before TLS termination fallback logic.
cheng: also run this probe from multiple egress IPs to verify: `python -c "import socket,ssl; s=socket.create_connection(('alb-eu-west',443)); ss=ssl.create_default_context().wrap_socket(s,server_hostname='api.prod.redwood.example'); print(ss.selected_alpn_protocol())"`
oliver: i'll coordinate with infra to pause EIP rotations for pool A for the next 6 hours.
oncall-liz: thanks. please post findings and timeline so SRE/Customer Success can notify impacted customers. :loudspeaker:
maria: updating INF-4321 with reproducer, pcap and clienthello dumps. will follow up with RCA once we confirm NAT resegmentation is root cause.
cheng: also want to try a short experiment — deploy small envoy edge (in front of ALB) with `reuse_port` disabled and reassembly enabled to see if it masks the issue. if envoy normalizes segments, that would prove resegmentation theory.
maria: noted. assigning envoy experiment to oliver.
oliver: on it, will post logs here.
maria: thanks everyone, keeping this thread for updates.
